text:
Buffalo took the lead on a 6 percent chance, a Tage Thompson power-play wrist shot at 8:00 of the first, and then watched Utah spend the rest of the night taking the game back. Kailer Yamamoto tied it just over two minutes later on a 60 percent look, and the first period ended with Utah ahead 1.79 to 0.43 in expected goals, the quality of chances. The scoreboard said 1-1. The ice said something else.

The second period followed the same script. Nick Schmaltz scored on a power play at 15:23, and Anders Lee added a backhand at 17:24 that put Utah up 3-1. John Marino made it 4-1 early in the third on a power-play slap shot that carried only a 4 percent chance, one of the few Utah goals that came from the margins rather than the middle of the ice. Marino finished with a goal and an assist while playing 19:06, and Barrett Hayton set up two goals on a line that owned a 1.92 to 0.45 edge in expected goals.

Buffalo's best stretch came after the game was largely gone, as the Sabres out-created Utah 1.72 to 1.25 in the third. Colten Ellis allowed four goals on 4.42 expected, so the damage was about what the shots deserved. Karel Vejmelka stopped 29 of 30 against 2.79 expected goals, a gap of 1.79 goals in Utah's favor. Utah won 74 percent of simulated replays of every shot, so this was a deserved win, and Vejmelka's night made it look cleaner than the chances alone would have.
